judgements.reason: Grothendieck-Euler-forms has its whole spine in the library (ExactStructure, PresentedK0, resolutionEquiv, cartanMap, extEulerPairing) and what is left - Cartan matrices in bases, resolving subcategories, bounded-complex/derived comparisons, q = +-1 specialization - is one step from what exists, whereas the quiver roadmap still needs the surjective half of Gabriel's bijection, the presentation theorem A = kQ/I, and the whole of Auslander-Reiten theory (AR duality, existence of almost-split sequences, the AR quiver) which its own document calls a formalization project in its own right.

Both are close: the quiver roadmap's path algebras, Krull-Schmidt, reflection functors and isFiniteRepType_of_titsForm_posDef are built and only Gabriel's converse plus AR theory remain, while Mathlib already holds CA.0-CA.5 (reciprocity, Moebius inversion, Pell, Bernoulli, Mahler measure, class groups); classical arithmetic is farther because higher reciprocity needs Hilbert symbols and explicit class field theory (absent), and CA.7 needs the whole integral Galois-module theory - locally free class groups over group rings, Noether and Hilbert-Speiser - together with canonical heights imported from ArithmeticDynamics.

Classical arithmetic mostly extends APIs Mathlib already has, its genuinely new pieces (Hilbert symbols, Smith/Hermite forms, Pisot-Salem bounds, tame normal-integral-basis theory) being broad but shallow; the p-adic L-function roadmap must build every one of its five stacked layers - the smoothed measure F_a and its Amice inverse, the pseudo-measure zeta_p with Kummer congruences, twists at arbitrary tame conductor, the p-adic logarithm and Leopoldt's formula, the Eisenstein measures - on top of Iwasawa-algebra measures, locally analytic distributions and the continuation of zeta_K, none of which exists.

Close call: the p-adic L-function roadmap at least starts from Mathlib's Mahler basis, Amice transform and Dirichlet L-function continuation, and its missing work is one connected analytic theory; the Galois-representation roadmap has seven separate absent bodies - invariant lattices and Brauer-Nesbitt, Weil groups and Weil-Deligne representations, Artin/Swan conductors (for which the upper-numbering ramification filtration does not exist in either tree), PGL2 finite-subgroup classification, Chebotarev recognition, polarizations and adequacy, Tate modules - and it additionally consumes Chenevier determinants from IHG.1.

Both build arithmetic theory on carriers that exist, but the determinant roadmap sits on a missing foundation the Galois-representation roadmap does not need: its IHG.3 spherical Hecke polynomial requires the Satake transform and the smooth representation theory of p-adic reductive groups (zero hits for 'Satake' and 'smooth representation' in either tree, plus the seven-stage ReductiveGroupsPartII import), and IHG.6 is the 2023 Dasgupta-Kakde-Silliman-Wang theorem, on top of the Cayley-Hamilton/generalized-matrix-algebra reconstruction that ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations merely consumes.

The determinant roadmap needs polynomial laws (Mathlib has a start), Cayley-Hamilton reconstruction, Satake normalization over an unbuilt p-adic-group tower and the DKSW Ribet theorem - seven layers of algebra; grid homology has its chain-level carriers built but still owes a larger body of new mathematics: d^2 = 0 in general, pentagon/hexagon invariance, GH^- as an F[U]-module and tau, the Milnor conjecture, the slice-genus bound via cobordism normal forms, Legendrian invariants, sign assignments, filtered complexes, Nemethi's Z[U] lattice homology and the whole of Lane H.

Grid homology's ground floor is already in Tau Ceti (grid complexes, gradings, the determinant formula, the plumbing lattice complex), so its very large remainder is theorems on existing carriers; complex comparison has no ground floor at all - complex analytic spaces and analytification have zero hits in both trees - and must build analytic coherence (Oka), Cartan-Serre finiteness, projective and proper GAGA, plus the algebraic side it presumes (O(n), projective morphisms, higher direct images, Chow's lemma, algebraic spaces) before the de Rham-Betti comparison can even be stated.

Complex comparison needs one coherent classical package - analytic spaces, coherence, GAGA, Chow, algebraic de Rham - over a single unbuilt upstream roadmap; effective Diophantine methods needs LLL (absent), certified algebraic numbers, explicit Baker-Matveev archimedean and p-adic linear forms in logarithms, S-unit and Thue-Mahler algorithms, saturation and Sha, higher-genus Jacobians, the whole of Coleman integration, Chabauty-Coleman, the Mordell-Weil sieve and quadratic Chabauty with Selmer varieties: a closure of 196 stages over 45 roadmaps at depth 17.

Modular symbols must build one well-delimited tower - symbols and parabolic cohomology, Eichler-Shimura periods, p-stabilization, Stevens' control theorem - over DirichletPadicLFunctions and locally analytic distributions (57 stages, 15 roadmaps); effective Diophantine methods stacks Baker-Matveev with explicit constants, LLL and certified arithmetic, Coleman integration, higher-genus Jacobians, the Mordell-Weil sieve and nonabelian Chabauty's unipotent fundamental groups, a closure more than three times as large and five layers deeper.

Modular symbols needs p-adic measures and distributions plus the eigencurve, but its objects are group-cohomological and Mathlib already supplies the modular-form L-function and Tau Ceti the Hecke operators; A_inf cohomology needs perfectoid spaces and almost purity, the pro-etale site with period sheaves, crystalline and de Rham-Witt cohomology, derived de Rham, the Fargues-Fontaine curve, prismatic cohomology and the THH bridge - none of 'crystalline', 'prismatic' or 'perfectoid space' exists - before L-eta, BKF modules and AOmega can be defined.

A_inf cohomology needs the integral p-adic Hodge tower (perfectoid spaces, pro-etale period sheaves, crystalline and derived de Rham, prismatic, Fargues-Fontaine); overconvergent forms need essentially that same p-adic Hodge input - its closure omits only ten stages of A_inf's - and then, on top of it, perfectoid Shimura varieties with the Hodge-Tate period map, canonical subgroups, Hilbert modular integral models and towers, toroidal compactifications and automorphic bundles, before the BHW coefficient sheaves, AIP comparison, U_p compactness and Hida comparison can start.

Both stack enormous towers: overconvergent forms wait on perfectoid Shimura varieties, Hodge-Tate period maps and Shimura compactifications, while p-adic local Langlands waits on Robba rings and (phi,Gamma)-modules with overconvergence and the Herr complex, p-adic Hodge theory, and classical smooth local Langlands for GL2 - none of which exists in either tree - and then owes Colmez's functor, admissible Banach and locally analytic categories, projective envelopes with deformation-ring comparisons and the Paskunas/Hu-Tan/Tung theorems including p = 2 and p = 3; its closure is larger (257 vs 217 stages) and six layers deeper.

P-adic local Langlands must build (phi,Gamma)-modules, the smooth/Banach/locally analytic representation theory of GL2(Q_p) and the Paskunas block machinery; Birch-Tate must build strictly more: the entire algebraic K-theory of rings of integers from nothing (no K-group above K_0, no Steinberg symbol or tame kernel in either tree), motivic and etale cohomology with the degree-two norm-residue comparison, the continuation and functional equation of zeta_F, the Iwasawa main conjecture with Kolster's implication, and all of the Kubota-Leopoldt theory, whose closure it contains outright.

Grothendieck-Euler forms is nearly finished in the library - exact structures, the four K_0s, the resolution theorem, cartanMap and the Ext-Euler pairing are all built and it imports nothing from other roadmaps; the determinant roadmap has none of its seven layers, and its Satake-normalized spherical Hecke polynomial additionally requires smooth representations of p-adic reductive groups and the Satake transform, which do not exist anywhere in either tree.

A_inf cohomology needs one (very large) p-adic tower - perfectoid, crystalline, derived de Rham, prismatic, Fargues-Fontaine - and Mathlib already supplies Witt vectors, perfection, theta and B_dR^+; Birch-Tate needs all of algebraic K-theory from K_2 upward with finiteness of the tame kernel, W_2 and w_2, the continuation and functional equation of zeta_F, the Iwasawa main conjecture and Kolster's implication, plus Kubota-Leopoldt and the regulator theories for its higher Lichtenbaum statements: a closure of 307 stages over 49 roadmaps against 97 over 20.

The quiver roadmap's foundations are in Tau Ceti - path algebras, the module equivalence, Krull-Schmidt, reflection functors, positive roots and the positive-definite half of Gabriel - so what remains is Gabriel's converse and Auslander-Reiten theory on built carriers; the p-adic L-function roadmap has no p-adic side at all: the smoothed measure, zeta_p, Kummer congruences, all-character twists, Leopoldt's formula and the Eisenstein measures, stacked on Iwasawa-algebra measures, locally analytic distributions and a continuation of zeta_K that the libraries do not have.

Grothendieck-Euler forms imports nothing and its remaining items (bounded-complex comparisons, resolving subcategories, Cartan matrices in bases, q = +-1 specialization) each sit one step from built theory; classical arithmetic, although Mathlib covers CA.0-CA.5, still owes power-residue and Hilbert symbols with a higher reciprocity law, Hermite/Smith/rational canonical forms, Christol's theorem, Smyth-Dobrowolski bounds and the whole integral Galois-module theory with locally free class groups, and it imports canonical heights and K_0 of group rings from two further roadmaps.

Arithmetic Galois representations builds seven classical bodies - lattices and Brauer-Nesbitt, Weil-Deligne, conductors, PGL2 images, Chebotarev recognition, Tate modules, adequacy - on carriers Mathlib and Tau Ceti already supply (continuous representations, the absolute Galois group, the cyclotomic character, Galois lattices); complex comparison has to create complex analytic spaces and analytification from nothing, then Oka coherence and Cartan-Serre finiteness, then GAGA and Chow, and separately the missing projective algebraic geometry (O(n), projective morphisms, higher direct images, Chow's lemma, algebraic spaces) before the de Rham-Betti theorem.

Grid homology owes a very large body of work, but its complexes, gradings, grid moves and plumbing lattices are already in Tau Ceti and it imports almost nothing; modular symbols has zero hits in either tree and its targets sit at the top of a twelve-deep chain none of whose links exists - Iwasawa-algebra measures, Kubota-Leopoldt, locally analytic distributions, modular symbols and Eichler-Shimura periods, Stevens' control theorem, and finally Bellaiche's critical-slope construction over the finite-slope eigenvariety.

Effective Diophantine methods needs Baker-Matveev with explicit constants, LLL, Coleman integration, higher-genus Jacobians and nonabelian Chabauty - 196 stages at depth 17; Birch-Tate needs more theory still: the whole of algebraic K-theory with K_2(O_F) and its finiteness, motivic and etale cohomology, the continuation and functional equation of zeta_F, the Iwasawa main conjecture over totally real fields and Kolster's implication, plus all of Kubota-Leopoldt, giving 307 stages over 49 roadmaps, 242 of them outside the Diophantine closure.

Modular symbols needs symbols and periods, p-stabilization and Stevens' control theorem over p-adic distributions and the eigencurve (57 upstream stages); p-adic local Langlands needs Robba rings and (phi,Gamma)-modules with overconvergence and the Herr complex, the full p-adic Hodge theory beneath them, classical smooth local Langlands for GL2, admissible Banach and locally analytic categories, Colmez's functor, projective envelopes and the Paskunas/Hu-Tan/Tung block theorems - 257 stages at depth 18.

Both are at the far end: overconvergent forms wait on perfectoid Shimura varieties, Hodge-Tate period maps, Hilbert integral models and compactifications before the BHW sheaves exist; Birch-Tate is farther by volume, needing the entire algebraic K-theory tower (K_2 and the tame kernel upward, with finite generation and the norm-residue comparison), the continuation and functional equation of zeta_F, the Iwasawa main conjecture and Kolster's implication, and all of the Dirichlet p-adic L-function theory, 249 of whose stages lie outside the overconvergent closure.

The quiver roadmap's path algebras, Krull-Schmidt, Euler and Tits forms, reflection functors and the positive-definite half of Gabriel are already in Tau Ceti, leaving Gabriel's converse and Auslander-Reiten theory; the determinant roadmap has none of its layers, and beyond Chenevier's polynomial-law and Cayley-Hamilton theory it needs the Satake transform and the smooth representation theory of p-adic reductive groups, the Chebotarev density theorem itself, and the 2023 DKSW extension theorem.

Classical arithmetic is largely a matter of extending Mathlib APIs it already has (reciprocity, Moebius inversion, Pell, Bernoulli, Mahler measure, class groups), with a broad but shallow remainder; arithmetic Galois representations has none of its seven layers - invariant lattices and characteristic-p Brauer-Nesbitt, Weil groups and Weil-Deligne representations, Artin and Swan conductors with no upper-numbering ramification filtration to stand on, PGL2 image classification, Chebotarev recognition over Chenevier determinants, polarizations and adequacy, Tate modules with the Weil-pairing determinant.
